newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down after persistent sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down after persistent sales.

text.p: Hong Kong bullion took a battering on persistent sales throughout Thursday trade to end well below New York's Wednesday close, and prices were headed towards US$368-370 per ounce, gold traders said.
"We saw some stop-loss selling as people got rid of their long positions," said one gold trader at an international bank.
Others said that brisk sales from Australian producers had caught the market by surprise.
"Perhaps they think the markets will be relatively quiet with the Thursday and Friday U.S. Thanksgiving holiday," said one trader at a European bullion house.
Bullion ended at US$372.00/50 an ounce on Thursday against New York's US$373.10/60 close on Wednesday.
A senior gold trader said that producer hedging was putting pressure on the market.
While mining companies had varying hedging strategies, those that hadn't hedged before started to do so when the markets were on their way down, he said.
Others said talk of central bank sales out of Europe had kept the market on its downward trend.
"There is not much liquidity in the market to absorb the sales," said one gold trader.
Physical buying was said to be quiet as end-users were waiting for the downward price spiral to end.

Hong Kong's tael gold traded at a hefty premium to spot bullion and was quoted at the Hong Kong dollar per tael equivalent of US$372.80/373.30 per ounce, but traders were not willing to sell tael gold because they would lose money on high interest rates at the local gold exchange, dealers said.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +5.00 on Thursday from its previous fix at nil.
Local gold ended HK$16 lower at HK$3,437 a tael.
